# Screens in Google Stitch

Use this after the page map exists. Stitch draws screens. It does not decide the product.

## Before the first prompt

- [ ] The page map names every screen and who sees it
- [ ] The visual rules are written down: palette, type, what is forbidden
- [ ] One job per section. Spare copy. Details appear on hover or click
- [ ] The prompt is one screen, or one clickable flow. A pile of unrelated prompts does not become a prototype

## How to generate

1. Open one Stitch project. Set the platform to Web.
2. Generate the logo or the homepage first and leave it on the canvas.
3. Paste only the prompt body. Wait until that screen finishes. Then paste the next prompt in the same project.
4. For a clickable pass, use one prompt that names the screens and the links between them. Then press Play and click through.

## After it generates

- [ ] Walk every screen against the page map. Missing pages and extra pages both get written down
- [ ] A dropped or merged field is a note, not a doc change. The PRD, system design, database, and API change only when the human explicitly says so
- [ ] Record the prompt method and the visual decisions in the journey log

## The Wedding Home example

5–6 Oct 2026. Bone paper, charcoal, pewter, Inter, a quiet serif only for the homepage headline. No script type, no floral stock, no pink-and-gold invite look. Twenty-two separate prompts produced pictures and no clickable flow. One Web prompt, then Play, is the pass that connects the screens. Wine or burgundy was added later as the accent on the mark, buttons, countdown, and links. The human asked the prototype to count veg, non-veg, and Jain only. The locked docs still store four diet headcounts, including no onion-garlic. That doc stays until the human asks to change it.
